title: Isolate TF state per-tenant with lease-based locking + GPU subnet affinity for private installs
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: Customers running Private deployments reported long apply times and frequent terraform lock contention when multiple tenant teams concurrently change infra (GPU pools, network attachments). A single monolithic tfstate also makes targeted rollbacks and per-tenant upgrades risky. This PR introduces a tenant-isolated state layout plus a lease-based locking option tailored for on-prem/private installs, and extends the GPU nodepool module to support explicit subnet affinity mapping so GPU pools can be co-located with customer-provided subnets. The change includes: 1) New backend conventions: per-tenant state workspaces (backend template + naming), optional MinIO/GCS backend examples, and an on-prem Consul-session lease mechanism for state locks (fallback to S3/DynamoDB in cloud). 2) A migration helper (state-splitter) that generates per-tenant state snapshots and a dry-run plan for operator review. 3) Enhancements to modules/gpu-nodepool: subnet_affinity_map variable (az->subnet-id), preferred_host_pools flag, and ephemeral-ip allocation policy for burst pools. 4) Console/operator-facing docs (docs/migrations/tenant-state-split.md) and an upgrade checklist. 5) Tests and CI: terraform validate/fmt, unit tests for the migrator, and an e2e private-installer test that exercises nodepool creation with subnet affinity. Rollout plan: feature gate in values.yaml defaults to off; operators can enable per-cluster; run state-splitter in dry-run mode, review generated plans, then flip over. Rollback: state-splitter also emits rejoin plan to remerge per-tenant states back into the consolidated state in case of rollback. Impact: No forced downtime for runtime workloads; terraform apply ordering will change for operators who opt-in (see migration doc). Checklist: - [x] Implement per-tenant backend templates - [x] Consul lease-based locking implementation (on-prem) - [x] GPU nodepool subnet affinity variables and tests - [x] state-splitter tool + dry-run validation - [x] Docs + upgrade checklist - [x] CI green (after rerun)

review_conversation: Ethan Morales: Can we avoid adding another mandatory backend type? Suggest default is opt-in (enabled=false) and document both Consul and DynamoDB options.
Priya Nair (author): Agreed — made it opt-in. Consul lease is only used when operator flips enable_consul_lease=true. Added cloud-backed DynamoDB example in backends/README.
Lina Chen: The subnet_affinity_map looks good, but how does it interact with autoscaler labels? We should ensure node labels are set consistently so the operator can target pools.
Priya Nair: Added preferred_host_pools and label propagation in nodepool module. Updated examples and tests to verify labels are present after apply.
Samir Patel: Migrator output looked good in dry-run; one nit: include a 'reverse plan' file to make rollbacks explicit.
Priya Nair: Added rejoin plan output from state-splitter and a small helper script scripts/tfstate-merge.sh to make re-merging straightforward.
Lina Chen: CI e2e failed on first run (timing flake creating subnets). Reran pipeline and it passed. Approving after second green run.
Ethan Morales: Approve with minor doc suggestions.
Samir Patel: LGTM — merging when CI green.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash+merge by Lina Chen. Commit message consolidated feature list and migration instructions.
release_notes: Introduce optional tenant-isolated TF state layout with on-prem lease-based locking (Consul sessions) and a state-splitter migrator. GPU nodepool module gains subnet_affinity_map and preferred_host_pools to colocate GPU node pools with operator subnets. Migration tool emits dry-run and rejoin plans. Opt-in feature; see docs/migrations/tenant-state-split.md for rollout steps.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature by setting helm.redwoodOperator.featureFlags.tenantStateSplit=true and follow docs/migrations/tenant-state-split.md; run tooling/state-splitter in dry-run mode, verify plans, then run for real. For on-prem: deploy Consul cluster and set consul.address in backend config to enable lease locking. If rollback needed, use scripts/tfstate-merge.sh with rejoin plan output.
